newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh government ponders new foreign bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh government ponders new foreign bond issues.

text.p: Kazakhstan's government, which last year placed a successful Eurobond on international markets, could tap foreign markets again this year, Daniar Abulgazin, Deputy Chairman of the Treasury, said on Tuesday.
"I do not conceal the fact that the government is now studying the possibility of placing another issue of its securities on international financial markets," he told Reuters.
Last December Kazakhstan's $200 million debut Eurobond, twice as large as initially planned, was snapped up on international markets.
ABN AMRO led the oil-rich Central Asian republic's issue, priced to yield 9.3 percent or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes.
"I do not rule out the possibility that not Eurobonds but Samurais could be the new issue to be placed on international markets," Abulgazin said.
Samurai bonds are yen-denominated bonds issued in Japan by foreign borrowers.

Abulgazin declined to name the rough amount of an eventual issue or the date of the issue but said several large foreign banks had already offered to become the government's agent to place the new issue.
He said in the second quarter of this year the government could also issue two- or three-year interest-bearing government bonds, and part of the issue could be offered to foreigners.
"Foreign investors already show strong interest in the future issue of these bonds," Abulgazin said.
Currently foreign investors are entitled to buy no more than 15 percent on Kazakh three-month discount Treasury bills (GKOs) and just 30 percent of six- and 12-month papers.
"We favour foreigners' purchases of longer-term papers ... we should also give a chance to local banks to adapt to new market environments through buying government securities," Abulgazin said.
